proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2. It supplies the density-one property of H^n on a rectifiable carrier (the part of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 ⇒ / Remark 1.5(3) used through "1.9 of Ch. 3") directly from Lipschitz graphs of arbitrarily small slope, using only Lipschitz image bounds for H^n and the Lebesgue density theorem (no area formula). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (= c_n · μH[n] for a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞), Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def); ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure L^n := volume; ω := unitBallVolume n = L^n(ball 0 1) ∈ (0, ∞); B_r(y) := closedBall y r; λ := H^n.restrict A; for P ∈ G := Grassmannian N n, p_P := Grassmannian.project P; densityRatio n λ x r = λ(B_r(x))/(ω · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n).

0. λ(ℝ^N) = H^n(A) < ∞, so λ is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure. Since A is H^n-null-measurable, λ-a.e. point lies in A (ae_restrict_mem₀).

1. Case n = 0. μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), μH[0]{a} = 1 (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), and finite sets are Borel, so H^0(F) = #F for every finite F ⊆ ℝ^N; if A were infinite it would contain finite subsets of every cardinality, contradicting H^0(A) < ∞. Hence A is finite. Moreover ω = unitBallVolume 0 = 1: ball 0 1 is the whole zero-dimensional space and volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is the Dirac mass at 0 (Mathlib volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac). For x ∈ A choose r_x > 0 smaller than the distance from x to every other point of A (r_x := 1 if A = {x}); for 0 < r < r_x, λ(B_r(x)) = H^0(A ∩ B_r(x)) = H^0({x}) = 1 (Measure.restrict_apply, B_r(x) closed), so densityRatio 0 λ x r = 1/(1 · 1) = 1. Thus HasDensity 0 λ x 1 for every x ∈ A, hence for λ-a.e. x by 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

2. Graph geometry. Fix L ∈ (0, 1], c = (P, Γ) ∈ C_L, p := p_P and β := (1 + L²)^{1/2}. projectionLinearMap P is symmetric and idempotent, so |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|² and |p v| ≤ |v|; hence for y, z ∈ Γ: |p y − p z| ≤ |y − z| and |y − z|² = |p(y − z)|² + |(y − z) − p(y − z)|² ≤ (1 + L²)|p y − p z|², i.e. |y − z| ≤ β |p y − p z|. So p is injective on Γ, and h := Function.invFunOn p Γ satisfies h(p y) = y on Γ and is β-Lipschitz on p(Γ). Put A_c := A ∩ Γ.

3. Comparison with the projection. Let x ∈ A_c, r > 0 and s := r/β. Then (a) p(A_c) ∩ B_s(p x) ⊆ p(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ⊆ p(A_c) ∩ B_r(p x) [if a = p z with z ∈ A_c and |a − p x| ≤ s, then |z − x| ≤ β s = r; conversely |p z − p x| ≤ |z − x|], and (b) A_c ∩ B_r(x) = h(p(A_c ∩ B_r(x))). H^n does not increase under the 1-Lipschitz map p and increases at most by the factor β^n under h, which is β-Lipschitz on p(Γ) ⊇ p(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le and LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:745 and 733, valid for arbitrary sets; they transfer to μHE[n] through the constant c_n). Therefore
 (∗) H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(p x)) ≤ H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ β^n H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_r(p x)).

4. Lebesgue density in the plane. Let e : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P.plane be a linear isometry equivalence (finrank P.plane = n, Grassmannian.finrank_plane) and ι := Subtype.val ∘ e, an isometry ℝ^n → ℝ^N with range P.plane. For every B ⊆ ℝ^n, H^n(ι(B)) = L^n(B) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:131 and 187). Put S := ι⁻¹(p(A_c)); since p(A_c) ⊆ P.plane = range ι we have ι(S) = p(A_c), and for b ∈ ℝ^n and s > 0, ι(S ∩ B_s(b)) = p(A_c) ∩ B_s(ι b) (ι is injective, isometric and onto P.plane); hence H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(ι b)) = L^n(S ∩ B_s(b)), while L^n(B_s(b)) = ω s^n (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). By the Lebesgue density theorem for arbitrary sets (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for L^n and S, Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1105), L^n(S ∩ B_s(b))/L^n(B_s(b)) → 1 as s ↓ 0 for (L^n.restrict S)-a.e. b; choose a Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^n containing all exceptional points with (L^n.restrict S)(E) = L^n(E ∩ S) = 0. Let N_c := ι(E ∩ S) ⊆ p(A_c). Then H^n(N_c) = L^n(E ∩ S) = 0, and for every a ∈ p(A_c) ∖ N_c (a = ι b with b ∈ S ∖ E): H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(a))/(ω s^n) → 1 as s ↓ 0. Finally X_c := {x ∈ A_c : p x ∈ N_c} ⊆ h(N_c), so H^n(X_c) ≤ β^n H^n(N_c) = 0.

5. Two-sided bounds. Let x ∈ A_c ∖ X_c; then a := p x ∈ p(A_c) ∖ N_c, and by (∗) and 4 (with s = r/β, so ω s^n = β^{−n} ω r^n):
 liminf_{r↓0} H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n) ≥ β^{−n} and limsup_{r↓0} H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n) ≤ β^n.
 In particular H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) > 0 for all small r > 0.

6. Density of Γ for λ. By Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for the finite measure λ and the set Γ: for (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x, λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x))/λ(B_r(x)) → 1 as r ↓ 0. Since Γ and B_r(x) are closed, λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x)) = H^n(Γ ∩ B_r(x) ∩ A) = H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Moreover λ.restrict Γ = H^n.restrict (Γ ∩ A) (Measure.restrict_restrict, Γ Borel); Γ ∩ A is H^n-null-measurable, so (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x lies in A_c, and (λ.restrict Γ)(X_c) ≤ H^n(X_c) = 0.

7. Combining. For (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x we therefore have x ∈ A_c ∖ X_c together with the convergence in 6. For small r, λ(B_r(x)) < ∞ and λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x)) = H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) > 0 (by 5), so λ(B_r(x))/(ω r^n) = [λ(B_r(x))/λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x))] · [H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n)], where the first factor tends to 1; by 5,
 β^{−n} ≤ liminf_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ limsup_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ β^n.

8. All of A. W_L := ⋃_{c ∈ C_L} c.2 is a countable union of closed sets, hence Borel, and A ⊆ W_L; so λ(ℝ^N ∖ W_L) = H^n((ℝ^N ∖ W_L) ∩ A) = 0 and λ = λ.restrict W_L. By ae_restrict_biUnion_iff / ae_restrict_iUnion_iff (C_L countable) and 7, the bounds of 7 with β = (1 + L²)^{1/2} hold for λ-a.e. x. (If C_L = ∅ then A = ∅, λ = 0, and everything is trivial.)

9. Apply 8 with L = 1/l for l = 1, 2, … and intersect the countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for λ-a.e. x and every l, (1 + l^{−2})^{−n/2} ≤ liminf_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ limsup_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ (1 + l^{−2})^{n/2}. Letting l → ∞ gives liminf = limsup = 1, hence densityRatio n λ x r → 1 as r ↓ 0 (tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup), i.e. HasDensity n λ x 1. ∎
key_steps: n = 0: A is finite, ω_0 = 1, so the density of H^0⌞A is 1 at each point of A.
On a closed L-graph Γ over P: |p y − p z| ≤ |y − z| ≤ (1+L²)^{1/2}|p y − p z|; p injective with (1+L²)^{1/2}-Lipschitz inverse h.
Lipschitz image bounds: H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_{r/β}(px)) ≤ H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ β^n H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_r(px)).
Lebesgue density theorem in the plane through an isometry ℝ^n → P.plane; the exceptional set pulls back to an H^n-null set via h.
Besicovitch density of the closed set Γ for λ = H^n⌞A converts H^n(A ∩ Γ ∩ B_r) into λ(B_r).
Countable union over C_L gives bounds (1+L²)^{∓n/2} λ-a.e.; L = 1/l → 0 gives density 1.
